title: A Full-Spectrum Theory of Moiré Superlattices
authors: Tong Liu, X. R. Wang, Jiansheng Wu
abstract: Conventional theoretical descriptions of moiré superlattices, epitomized by the Bistritzer--MacDonald continuum model, are fundamentally constrained by low-energy Dirac cone approximations and first-shell interlayer coupling truncations. While successful for small-angle twisted bilayer graphene near charge neutrality, these frameworks fail to provide universal analytical solutions for strained lattices, high-energy band behaviors, or arbitrary commensurate geometries. Here, we establish a unified, approximation-free analytical formalism for generalized moiré systems based on three pillars: (i) a rigorous two-dimensional-to-one-dimensional supercell cyclic mapping, (ii) exact block-circulant diagonalization of intralayer Hamiltonians, and (iii) quasi-degenerate Löwdin perturbation theory centered on arbitrary energy degeneracy points across the full spectrum. Unlike traditional schemes anchored to the Dirac point, our approach enables systematic perturbative expansions around any band crossing, unifying the characterization of low-energy flat bands with high-energy degeneracies. We demonstrate that this framework perfectly recovers the Bistritzer--MacDonald model in the low-energy limit while extending its reach to heterostrained systems and high-energy regimes. By incorporating high-order interlayer coupling shells, we reveal an intrinsic scale self-similarity in moiré lattices and predict the emergence of higher-order magic angles and tunable flat bands driven by secondary degeneracies. This work eliminates the long-standing lack of universal analytical tools for diverse moiré platforms, providing a full-spectrum theoretical foundation for band engineering and the exploration of exotic correlated and topological states in van der Waals heterostructures.
summary: This paper introduces a comprehensive, approximation-free theoretical framework for analyzing moiré superlattices, overcoming the limitations of models based solely on low-energy Dirac cones. By employing a novel combination of cyclic mapping, block-circulant diagonalization, and generalized perturbation theory, the authors can accurately model the full electronic spectrum. This work provides a universal tool for engineering band structures in diverse van der Waals heterostructures.
main_problem: Conventional theoretical models for moiré superlattices are limited by low-energy approximations and truncated interlayer couplings, failing to describe high-energy or strained geometries.
main_result: The authors establish a unified, approximation-free analytical formalism that extends beyond the Dirac point to characterize flat bands and degeneracies across the full energy spectrum.
method: The formalism uses a rigorous 2D-to-1D supercell cyclic mapping combined with exact block-circulant diagonalization and quasi-degenerate Löwdin perturbation theory.
model_or_system: The system is a general moiré superlattice described by a block Hamiltonian, which is analyzed by mapping the lattice structure onto a 1D cyclic supercell geometry.
key_observables: Flat band characteristics, high-energy degeneracies, and the full energy spectrum of the system.
important_parameters: The analysis is sensitive to the degree of strain, the inclusion of high-order interlayer coupling shells, and the energy point around which perturbation theory is centered.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is that the Hamiltonian can be mapped onto a block-circulant structure due to the cyclic reordering of unit cells.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the Moiré superlattice structure, the general block matrix Hamiltonian, and the resulting band structures for 1D chain models.
paper_structure: The paper develops a comprehensive theoretical framework by first identifying the limitations of existing models, then introducing the three pillars of the new formalism (mapping, diagonalization, perturbation theory), and finally demonstrating its applicability across various physical regimes.
why_interesting: The development of a universal, full-spectrum theoretical tool for moiré systems is highly relevant for understanding emergent correlated and topological states in van der Waals heterostructures, bridging low-energy physics with high-energy band structure.
